Date: 2027-05-04T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up — pilot approach

Hi Aditya — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can lock the pilot timeline:

- Priority use case: patient intake summarization + triage suggestion (we care about hallucination rate and latency under load)
- Success signals: 90% accuracy on triage labels vs. clinician adjudication (sample n=200), median 95th-pctile latency < 450ms at 6 rps, no PHI stored beyond session retention window
- Data: we'll provide de-identified sample transcripts (about 250 records) by end of week

Can you confirm Redwood's proposed evaluation cadence and which of your team will own the runbook and decision readout? Also attaching a quick success-criteria spreadsheet for alignment.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Huang
Director of Clinical Product, NexaHealth

Attachment: Nexa_POC_success_criteria.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@nexahealth.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@nexahealth.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-04T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up — pilot approach

Claire — great summary, and thanks for the attachment. Short answers and proposed plan below.

Recap / confirmation:
- Use case and primary success signals: agreed on the triage accuracy target and latency SLO. We'll treat data retention as a gating compliance item — see notes on retention below.

Proposed evaluation sprint (2 weeks):
1) Week 0 (prep, 2–3 days): data ingestion + validation, sandbox model selection (open model variants), baseline metrics
2) Week 1 (run): 3 phased runs — low-load functional checks, scaled run to 6 rps, manual adjudication sample collection
3) Week 2 (analysis + readout): metric aggregation, failure-mode analysis, executive readout prep

Ownership:
- Redwood runbook & execution: Soojin Lee (SE) — owns ingestion, model config, and run execution
- Customer clinical validation coordination + adjudication samples: Claire / Tom
- Success-metrics analysis & exec deck: Marissa Cole (CS)

Decision process / readout:
- We propose an internal exec readout with Nexa stakeholders and Redwood sales + CS (30–45m) to review results. Go/No-go based on the pre-agreed spreadsheet thresholds (attached). If green, we move to contract SOW + reserved capacity sizing.

Compliance note:
- We will not persist raw transcripts in our hosted environment beyond the agreed retention window. If you need customer-managed private deployment for data residency, we can scope Redwood Private (we should discuss by Tuesday).

Next concrete steps (this week):
- Claire: share de-identified samples by 2027-05-06 EOD
- Soojin: provide ingestion spec + test account by 2027-05-05
- Marissa: draft exec-readout agenda and decision checklist by 2027-05-07

I'll follow up with a calendar poll for the executive readout window.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Readout agenda (30–45m):
1) Quick demo & live sample (5–8m)
2) Metrics snapshot vs. success spreadsheet (10m)
3) Failure-mode highlights + root cause (10m)
4) Recommendation & commercial next step (SOW sizing, Private vs Dedicated) (7–12m)

Decision rubric (pre-agreed):
- Pass: meets triage accuracy threshold AND latency target at 6 rps; recommended to proceed to SOW + reserved capacity sizing.
- Conditional pass: meets one target but not the other; recommend targeted remediation plan and follow-up micro-run.
- Fail: fails both; recommend revisit architecture or scope smaller bounded use-case.

- Claire / Tom: confirm exec attendees and preferred slot by 2027-05-08
